primitives.description: Pure, reusable building blocks without side effects.

rules.description: Primitives MUST NOT perform I/O or have side effects
Primitives MUST be deterministic and pure
Kernel contains orchestration only, no business rules
Kernel owns and controls system lifecycle states
Kernel MUST NOT contain domain or business logic

core_modules.description: Domain-neutral infrastructure abstractions with stable contracts.

rules.description: Core modules MUST NOT depend on specific frameworks
Core modules MUST declare explicit dependencies
Core modules define contracts, not concrete implementations
Adapters MUST NOT implement business or domain logic
Adapters MUST be thin translation layers only
Adapters ARE framework-specific and replaceable
Core modules MUST NOT depend on adapters

extensions.description: Optional enterprise-grade policies and operational concerns.

rules.description: Extensions MUST be optional and composable
Extensions implement policy, not abstraction
Extensions MUST NOT modify kernel behavior
Application layer owns configuration and environment resolution
Application layer defines orchestration and wiring
Application layer contains business rules and use cases
All errors MUST extend BaseError
Error codes MUST be namespaced (module:reason)
Each module MUST expose a finite Reason union
Error messages MUST be safe to log (no sensitive data)
Each module MUST expose exactly one public error class
HTTP status in meta is a hint, not a dependency

errors.note: Comity uses exceptions for failures. For expected failures, the error model provides structured metadata via reason and code. Result<T,E> pattern may be considered for future enhancements.

rules.description: Commands MUST be immutable DTOs with no behavior
Commands MUST contain only serializable data
Each command MUST have exactly one handler in Application Layer
Command handlers MUST return Result<T,E>
Commands MUST NOT throw; handlers MAY throw only for programmer errors
Commands MAY produce events; events MUST NOT produce commands
Events are observational and MUST NOT influence control flow
System MUST function correctly without event listeners
Event payloads MUST be safe to log (identifiers, not objects)
Event names MUST be verbs in past tense
Hooks are participatory and MAY influence control flow
Hook execution order MAY matter and MUST be defined
Hooks are part of lifecycle contracts

separation_rule.description: Events MUST NOT trigger hooks; Hooks MAY emit events

rules.description: Configuration MUST be owned by Application Layer
Configuration MUST be typed and immutable
Configuration MUST be injected explicitly, never read from globals
Configuration MUST be validated at bootstrap; invalid config fails fast
Environment resolution happens once at application boundary
Configuration objects MUST NOT be mutated at runtime
Public APIs MUST be intentional, stable, and documented
Internal APIs MUST NOT be exported or documented
Behavior exposure SHOULD use Facade pattern
Sub-entrypoints MUST represent clear conceptual domains
Breaking changes MUST be rare, justified, and documented
Promotion to core module is rare and requires architectural review
Extension must be production-proven across multiple systems, stable, and framework-agnostic
Core modules define abstraction; extensions define policy
Promoted modules must have versioned API, compliant error model, acyclic dependencies, and complete documentation
Tests MUST validate contracts and behavior, not implementations
Testing approach MUST vary by architectural layer
Primitives MUST NEVER be mocked in tests of other layers - they are foundation
Kernel MUST NEVER be mocked in tests of other layers - it is foundation
Core modules MAY use mocks only for declared dependencies
Adapter tests MUST use real frameworks, never mocks
Extensions tests SHOULD use mocks at module boundaries
Application layer tests MAY use mocks at layer boundaries
Mocks MUST mock contracts, not internal details
All fields MUST be declared explicitly (no parameter properties)
Internal state MUST use #private JavaScript fields
Public state MUST be exposed via getters
Constructor MUST fully initialize the instance
Field initializers are FORBIDDEN except for constants
Classes with phases MUST use Lifecycle abstraction
Classes MUST throw only BaseError or subclasses

infrastructure_logic.description: Non-business logic required to enforce protocol, runtime safety, or invariants.

rules.description: Infrastructure logic (middleware flow control, protocol invariants, safety checks) is NOT business logic
Infrastructure logic MAY live in internal/, middleware/, pipeline/, or facade implementations
Infrastructure logic MUST NOT be confused with or replace domain logic
README.md MUST follow standard structure (Purpose, Scope, Public API)
Detailed documentation MUST live in docs/ directory
Design decisions documented as topic files, not formal ADRs
Only current decisions are kept; deprecated decisions are deleted
All public APIs MUST be documented
Internal APIs MUST NOT be documented
Dependencies MUST flow: Application → Extensions → Adapters → Core Modules → Kernel
Reverse dependencies are forbidden
Kernel MUST NOT import any other internal package
Core modules MUST NOT depend on adapters
Adapters MAY depend on exactly one core module
Architectural boundaries MUST be clear and enforced
Public contracts MUST be stable and versioned
Adapters MUST be thin, framework-specific, and replaceable
Modules MUST be composable and explicitly declare dependencies
Kernel orchestrates, modules provide functionality, adapters translate
All behavior MUST be visible in code; no implicit magic
Enterprise-grade means deterministic, safe defaults, structured failure

terms.core_module: Domain-neutral infrastructure abstraction with stable contract
terms.adapter: Framework-specific translation layer between Comity and external world
terms.extension: Optional cross-cutting policy (rate limiting, tracing, retry)
terms.application_layer: Business logic, composition, and configuration owner
terms.command: Immutable DTO representing an imperative operation
terms.event: Observational signal describing something that happened
terms.hook: Participatory extension point that MAY influence control flow
terms.facade: Public API that hides orchestration complexity
